title: extract_with_repair output
description: Output for extract_with_repair. `extraction` is the LAST attempt's record, null when no attempt produced one. `valid` is true only when that record exists, the validator accepted it AND no issue remains — an unresolved issue can never travel beside `valid: true`. `attempts` records every engine call (one, or two when the first was rejected with findings), so a caller can see that the repair happened rather than trusting `repaired`. An engine failure is raised as an error, never reported as an empty record here.

extraction.description: The last attempt's record, verbatim from the engine, or null when none was produced. Never an empty object standing in for a failure. The record's own fields are governed by the caller's schema; the host's schema DSL cannot advertise `additionalProperties` on a union-typed node, so it is deliberately not repeated here (structured_extract's output schema has the same shape for the same reason).

valid.description: Whether the last attempt is admissible: an extraction exists, the validator accepted it, and it reported no issue.

issues.description: The LAST attempt's violations, so a caller sees what still fails after the repair. Empty exactly when `valid` is true.

repaired.description: Whether a second engine call actually ran. False means one attempt was enough or, for a 'nothing matched' answer, that no finding existed to repair.

attempts.description: One entry per engine call, oldest first. Never longer than two: this tool makes an initial attempt and at most one repair.

allOf.description: A positive verdict carries a record and no unresolved issue. A schema cannot correlate fields without this conditional; the package enforces the same rule in code.
`repaired` and the attempt list must agree: two attempts mean a repair ran, one means it did not.

valid.description: Whether this attempt was an admissible extraction.

meta.description: The host stamps this envelope. The provider never authors it (EXT-17).
